clip_script:
Now the recipe needs one sixth of a cup. Divide one by six. Six into ten is one, remainder four; into forty, six, remainder four; into forty, six, remainder four — forever. Zero comma one six six six six, with the six repeating. It never stops, because six has a three in it, and threes never divide neatly into tens. On the jug you fill to about zero comma one seven, and you say about, because the true value is a sixth and the decimal is only an approximation.

Here is a quick way to predict which kind of fraction you have, before dividing. Look at the bottom number. If it is made only of twos and fives — two, four, five, eight, ten, sixteen, twenty, twenty-five — the decimal will stop. If it has a three or a seven or an eleven in it — three, six, seven, nine, twelve, fifteen — the decimal will go on forever.
visual_style: Long division unrolling forever beside one that stops; a bank statement and a measuring jug
pacing: steady, with a beat as the remainder repeats
